messages:
mina: Ran onboarding eval for orion-v3:int6 on the mixed CJK+AR subtitle suite. Observed parentheses flipping around Arabic spans embedded in Japanese quotes. chrF down ~6 vs fp16 for a small subset. Repro: `./evals/run.py --suite locale/cjk_ar_mixed --model orion-v3 --quant int6 --seed 7`

ci-bot: CI job `evals/cjk-ar-onboard/2820000001` finished with regressions. Artifacts: /ci/artifacts/2820000001/report.html

kai: Reproed locally. FP16 output preserves parentheses orientation; int6 output shows mirrored parens: e.g. expected "(مرحبا)" becomes ")مرحبا(" after detok.

andre: Paste tiny example? is this detokenizer mirroring or tokenization boundary issue?

mina: Example:
```
# src: "彼はこう言った (مرحبا)"
# fp16: "彼はこう言った (مرحبا)"
# int6: "彼はこう言った )مرحبا("
```

dana: Suspect: int6 detok picked up detok v2.6 with "smart-mirror" behavior. fp16 used v2.4. If detok changed mirroring heuristics it could flip neutrals when adjacent run classes differ.

kai: I checked token dumps: tokens cross script boundary so run segmentation differs slightly in int6 build. directionality markers show AL for Arabic run and ON for parens. Post-detok mirroring step flips them.

andre: Quick mitigation: routing pin affected customers to fp16 or enable a post-detok scrub that prefers neutral orientation when mixed-script inside parens. e.g. `post_process.fix_bidi_parens: true`.

mina: I'll open PR with failing unit test and pin detok to v2.4 in int6 artifact to confirm. Also running bisect: `tools/bisect_detok.sh --range v2.4..v2.6 --model orion-v3 --quant int6`.

dana: Tagging @oncall-ml. Customer comms: offer pin to fp16 for the small percentage of affected captions.

kai: Will follow up with bisect results. If detok is root cause we revert roll-forward; if tokenization boundary is root cause we regenerate merges for quant build.
